title: 8 Cleaning Tools That Make Cleaning Easier to Start (Amazon Finds)
description: 8 Amazon cleaning tools that remove setup and make chores quicker to start, plus where to keep them so you actually use them.
intro:
Here's a secret about cleaning with an ADHD brain: the hard part is rarely the cleaning. It's everything *before* the cleaning. Find the vacuum. Untangle the cord. Fill the bucket. Find the good cloth. By then, the energy is gone.

So the best cleaning tools aren't the most powerful ones. They're the ones with the least setup, the ones you can grab and use in under ten seconds.

Here are eight tools that shrink the "getting ready" part down to almost nothing, plus a few tips on where to keep them.

sections.heading: The 10-second rule
sections.body:
When you're choosing a cleaning tool, ask: can I go from "I noticed a mess" to "I'm cleaning it" in ten seconds?

- Cordless beats corded.
- Spray mop beats bucket and mop.
- Soap-in-the-handle beats sponge plus bottle.
- A tool in every room beats one tool in the hall closet.

Every second of setup you remove makes the task more likely to happen.

sections.heading: Where you keep tools matters more than which tools
sections.body:
A handheld vacuum in the hall closet gets used once a month. The same vacuum mounted on the kitchen wall gets used every day.

Keep cleaning tools where messes happen:

- **Kitchen:** handheld vacuum, spray and cloths, dish brush.
- **Bathroom:** toilet brush, squeegee, a pack of wipes under the sink.
- **Living room:** a mini dustpan in a basket, a lint or pet hair roller.

Yes, that might mean owning two of something. That's okay. Two cheap tools that get used beat one fancy tool that doesn't.

sections.heading: Make tools easy to put away, too
sections.body:
A tool that's annoying to put back will end up leaning against a wall forever. Wall mounts, hooks and caddies help. The spray mop hangs on a hook. The handheld vacuum lives on its charger. The cloths go in a small bin.

If putting a tool away takes one motion, you'll do it.

sections.heading: The grab-and-go caddy
sections.body:
For bigger cleans, keep a caddy stocked with your essentials: one all-purpose spray, a glass cleaner, cloths, a scrub brush and a few trash bags. Carry the whole caddy from room to room.

This stops the "walk to the kitchen to get something, get distracted by the kitchen, forget about the bathroom" loop. We all know that loop.

sections.heading: Color-code your cloths
sections.body:
Microfiber cloths in different colors take all the thinking out of which cloth goes where. Pick a simple rule, like blue for glass, green for kitchen, pink for bathroom, and you'll never have to wonder whether that cloth was used on the toilet.

Toss them in the wash, and they're ready again.

sections.heading: A quick word on gadgets
sections.body: It's easy to get excited about cleaning gadgets. (Guilty.) Before you buy one, ask: will I actually use this at least once a week? Will it replace something I already own? If the answer is no, it'll end up as clutter, and clutter is the opposite of what we're going for.

finds.name: Cordless handheld vacuum
finds.why: Grab, zap, done. No cord and no big vacuum means small messes get handled right away.

finds.name: Refillable spray mop
finds.why: No bucket to fill means mopping takes five minutes instead of a whole production.

finds.name: Soap-dispensing dish brush
finds.why: Soap lives in the handle, so rinsing one mug is one step instead of three.

finds.name: Color-coded microfiber cloths
finds.search: microfiber cleaning cloths color coded pack
finds.why: One color per room means no thinking. Grab, wipe, done.

finds.name: Cordless electric spin scrubber
finds.why: A spinning head takes the elbow grease out of tubs and grout, which makes starting easier.

finds.name: Shower squeegee with hook
finds.why: Hang it in the shower and swipe after showering. Future scrubbing drops way down.

finds.name: Mini dustpan and brush set
finds.why: Small enough to keep in every room, so small spills get swept up right away.

finds.name: Extendable microfiber duster
finds.search: extendable microfiber duster with long handle
finds.why: An extending handle reaches fans and shelf tops from the floor.

outro:
Pick the one task you avoid most. Then pick the tool that removes its setup. That's the one to try first.

And if you want a room-by-room list of which tools to keep where, it's inside *The Messy Brain Home Reset*.
